paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.
model_annotation: The diagram compares the Efficacy$_{top}$ and noise$_E$ of AlphaEdit and MEMIT methods for the GPT2-XL model. The x-axis represents the number of edits, ranging from 0 to 3000 with regular intervals of 500. The left y-axis measures Efficacy$_{top}$, spanning from 30 to 100, while the right y-axis measures noise$_E$, ranging from 0 to 140. AlphaEdit Efficacy$_{top}$ is depicted by a red dashed line, starting at approximately 99 at 500 edits and decreasing to around 87 at 3000 edits. MEMIT Efficacy$_{top}$ is shown as a blue dashed line, beginning at about 88 at 500 edits and dropping to roughly 10 at 3000 edits. AlphaEdit noise$_E$ is represented by a red solid line, starting at around 27 at 500 edits and increasing to approximately 30 at 3000 edits. MEMIT noise$_E$ is illustrated by a blue solid line, starting at about 29 at 500 edits and rising to around 145 at 3000 edits. The diagram effectively visualizes the changes in Efficacy$_{top}$ and noise$_E$ for both methods as the number of edits increases.
